statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-16389 is an integer overflow in NSS's CERT_Hexify(), which allocates three bytes per input byte for a hex string without guarding that multiplication; Mozilla fixed it in Firefox 153: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-68/#CVE-2026-16389. The fix, Mozilla bug 2043887, adds a check in lib/certhigh/certhtml.c that rejects an input longer than UINT_MAX / 3 before the allocation: https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/projects/nss/rev/9e854d9c6234. Debian fixed it in trixie in 2:3.110-1+deb13u4, DSA-6403-1, and lists 2:3.126-1 as the fixed version in unstable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-16389. The DHI Debian repository publishes four builds of nss for Debian 13: a rebuild of Debian's 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 and builds of NSS 3.131.1, 3.132 and 3.134. We checked the libnss3 package of each on amd64 and arm64, verified against the index checksums: in every one, the disassembled CERT_Hexify() in libnss3.so compares the input length with 0x55555555 (UINT_MAX / 3) before it allocates, and the libnssutil3.so version strings confirm NSS 3.110, 3.131.1, 3.132 and 3.134. As a control, CERT_Hexify() in Debian's unfixed libnss3 2:3.124-1 for arm64 has no such comparison. The changelog shipped in the 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 rebuild lists this CVE under Debian's 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 entry. Every published build carries the fix, so the range closes at the lowest published build, the 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 rebuild.
